part.text: Found it. In `streamTrim` (src/object.c:1074-1076), the ID deltas are read into 32-bit `int`s. When the master entry has a small ID (e.g. `10-1`) and later entries use auto-generated epoch-based IDs, the ms delta (1629903486160) overflows `int`, truncating the computed current ID so it appears lower than MINID — every entry then gets marked deleted.
The iterator is fine (`lpGetInteger` returns int64_t and is added directly). Only `streamTrim` truncates to `int`. Applying the fix:
Now build and verify with a reproduction:

part.text:
All stream tests pass.

**Root cause:** In `streamTrim` (src/object.c:1074-1076), the entry ID deltas read from the listpack were stored in 32-bit `int` variables. When a stream's master entry has a small ID (e.g. `10-1`) and later entries use auto-generated epoch-based IDs, the milliseconds delta (~1.6 trillion) overflows `int`, so the reconstructed entry ID appeared lower than the MINID threshold — causing `streamTrim` to mark every entry as deleted.

**Fix:** Changed `ms_delta`/`seq_delta` to `int64_t` (matching `lpGetInteger`'s return type, as already done correctly in the stream iterator and `lpGetEdgeStreamID`). Verified with the exact reproduction from the issue: XTRIM now removes only the two entries below the threshold, and `unit/type/stream` passes fully.
